To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the entire miRNA miR-379/656 cluster is a tumor-suppressor locus in human cancers, 2) the cluster is downregulated in multiple cancers, and 3) the downregulation is likely due to DNA methylation at the cluster and down-regulation of the transcription factor MEF2, which is a crucial regulator for the cluster.
The entire C14 miR cluster is downregulated in multiple cancers and is likely a tumor suppressor cluster.
the entire C-14 cluster of 43 miRNAs is down regulated in GBM, KIRC, OV, and BRCA, and that the C14 locus is hypermethylated in GBM patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the miR-379/656 cluster on chromosome 14 in the development of glioblastoma and other human cancers.
the identification of miRNA clusters in the human genome and the analysis of their coordinated regulation in human cancer.
the role of a specific miRNA cluster (miR-379/mir-656) in the development and progression of glioblastoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the miR-379-656 cluster is a tumor-suppressor locus that plays a role in the development and progression of GBM.
C14 is a tumour suppressor locus.

the miRNAs of the cluster C14 (miR-379/mir-656) are downregulated in multiple cancers, including glioblastoma, breast and kidney cancer, and that this down-regulation is likely caused by hyper-methylation and/or loss of the miRNA expression by the transcription factor MEF2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the miR-379-656 cluster as a tumor suppressor in several cancers, including GBM.
we have identified a tumor suppressor miRNA cluster in human cancers, especially in glioblastomas.
the entire C-14 cluster of miRNAs (miR-379/mir-656) is a tumor suppressive locus and that it is involved in multiple cancers especially in GBM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miRNAs in a cluster are likely to be coordinately regulated and function together in cancer.
miR-379 and miR-656 are significantly downregulated in human cancers, and this downregulation is likely to contribute to tumorigenesis.
